Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:10:1.hebrew: א"ה שפחה נמי - דולדה כמוה, תיפוק לן מהאי קרא, דהא לא קרינן בה "כי תהיין", כדכתיב (בראשית כ״ב:ה׳): "עם החמור" — עם הדומה לחמור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:10:1.english: If so, a maidservant too - That her offspring is like her, let us derive [it] from this verse, for we do not read in her case “If [a man] have [wives],” as it is written (Genesis 22:5): “With the donkey” — a people resembling a donkey.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:1:1.hebrew: האשה וילדיה וגו' - בשפחה כנענית שייחדה לעבד עברי, ואמר קרא דלא יצא הבן חפשי עם אביו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:1:1.english: “The wife and her children,” etc. - [This refers to] a Canaanite maidservant whom [the master] designated for a Hebrew slave; and Scripture states that the son shall not go out free with his father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:2:1.english: Neither shall you make marriages with them - You shall not have with them the legal status of marriage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:1.hebrew: כי יסיר את בנך - לעיל מיניה כתיב: ״בתך לא תתן לבנו ובתו לא תקח לבנך״, וסמיך ליה: ״כי יסיר את בנך״. מדלא כתיב ״כי יסיר את בתך״, משמע דבן הנולד לעובד כוכבים מבתך קאמר — שיסירנו העובד כוכבים מאחריו; ושמעינן דבן בתך, אפילו מן העובד כוכבים, קרוי בנך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:1.english: For he will turn away your son - Prior to it, it is written: “Your daughter you shall not give to his son, and his daughter you shall not take for your son,” and juxtaposed to it [is]: “For he will turn away your son.” Since it is not written, “For he will turn away your daughter,” it implies that it is speaking of the son born to the idolater from your daughter — that the idolater will turn him away from following Him; and we learn that your daughter’s son, even from an idolater, is called your son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:2.hebrew: ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך - מדלא כתיב נמי ״כי תסיר את בנך״, דנשמע מיניה דקפיד נמי קרא ב״בתו לא תקח לבנך״ משום ״כי תסיר״ את הבן הנולד לה מבנך — אלמא בן העובדת כוכבים אינו קרוי בנך, אלא בנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:2.english: And your son who comes from a gentile woman is not called your son - Since it is not also written: “For she will turn away your son,” from which we would understand that the verse is also concerned regarding “and his daughter you shall not take for your son,” because “she will turn away” the son born to her from your son — evidently, the son of a gentile woman is not called your son, but her son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:3.hebrew: בנך מישראלית קרוי בנך כו' - לאו מקרא דייק לה, אלא ה"ק: מדלא קפיד קרא אבן הנולד ממנה, ש"מ: בנך מישראלית קרוי בנך, אבל בנך מן העובדת כוכבים אינו בנך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:3:3.english: Your son from an Israelite woman is called your son, etc. - [The Gemara] does not infer this from the verse; rather, this is what it means: Since Scripture was not concerned about the son born from her, learn from this: your son from an Israelite woman is called your son, but your son from a gentile woman is not your son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:4:1.hebrew: ש"מ - מדקרי ליה לבן בת ישראל הבא מן העובד כוכבים "בנך":
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:4:1.english: Learn from this - Since [Scripture] calls the son of a Jewish woman born to a gentile “your son.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:4:2.hebrew: לימא קסבר רבינא עובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל הולד ממזר - גרסי'. דאתא לאשמועינן, דלא שדינן ליה בתר עובד כוכבים — דנימא עובד כוכבים הוא, ואם נתגייר יהא מותר לבא בקהל — אלא בתר ישראלית שדינן ליה; וכיון שבעבירה נולד, הוה ליה ישראל פסול כשאר נולדים ממי שאין עליו קידושין, דתנן במתני' (לעיל קידושין דף סו:) שהם ממזרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:4:2.english: Shall we say Ravina holds [that with regard to] a gentile or a slave who engaged in intercourse with a Jewish woman, the offspring is a mamzer? - This is our reading. For it comes to teach us that we do not assign him to follow the gentile — that we should say he is a gentile, and if he converts he would be permitted to enter the congregation — but rather, we assign him to follow the Jewish woman. And since he was born through a transgression, he is a disqualified Jew, like all others born of someone with whom betrothal cannot take effect, as we learned in the Mishnah (above 66b) that they are mamzerim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:5:1.hebrew: ומשני - מהכא לא תשמע ממזרות. נהי דשמעינן מינה דכשר לא הוי — מדשדי ליה בתר ישראל להיות נולד בעבירה — ממזר מיהא לא תשמע מינה, כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף מה:) דממזר מאשת אביו יליף: מה אשת אב דאין לו עליה קידושין אבל יש לו קידושין על אחרת, ועלה כתיב שהולד ממזר — דסמיך ליה ״לא יבא ממזר״ — אף כל שאין לו עליה קידושין אבל יש לו קידושין על אחרת, לאפוקי עובד כוכבים דלית ליה קידושין כלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:5:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: From here, you cannot deduce mamzer status. Although we learn from it that he is not fit, since [the verse] casts him after [the status of] an Israelite to be [considered] born of a transgression, nonetheless, [that he is a] mamzer you cannot deduce from it, as we say in Yevamot (45b) that [the definition of a] mamzer is derived from [the case of] his father's wife: Just as with his father's wife, [it is a union where] he cannot effect betrothal with her, but he can effect betrothal with another [woman], and regarding it, it is written that the offspring is a mamzer — for juxtaposed to it is: “A mamzer shall not enter” — so too, any [union] where he cannot effect betrothal with her, but he can effect betrothal with another [woman, produces a mamzer]; to the exclusion of a gentile, who has no [capacity for] betrothal at all.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:5:2.hebrew: פסול מיקרי - כשאר נולדים בעבירה — מחייבי לאוין או עשה — שאינן ממזרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:5:2.english: He is called disqualified - Like the rest of those born from a transgression — [from unions prohibited by] negative commandments or a positive commandment — who are not mamzerim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:6:1.hebrew: האי בשבעה אומות כתיב - ״לא תתחתן בם״ ו״כי יסיר״ — בשבעה גוים שבא"י הוא דכתיב. שאר אומות מנלן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:6:1.english: This is written regarding the seven nations - “You shall not make marriages with them” and “For he will turn away” are written regarding the seven nations that were in the Land of Israel; from where do we [derive this for] the other nations?

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:7:1.hebrew: דדריש טעמא דקרא - בב"מ (דף קטו.) גבי אלמנה, דקאמר: עשירה ממשכנין אותה, עניה לא ממשכנין אותה; דטעמא מאי אמר רחמנא "לא תחבול בגד אלמנה"? מפני שאתה צריך להחזיר לה עבוטה לערב, ומתוך כך שאתה יוצא ונכנס תמיד אצלה, שחרית למשכן וערבית להחזיר, אתה משיאה שם רע בשכנותיה. והכי נמי, דריש טעמא דחיתון משום "כי יסיר", ולא איצטריך קרא לפרושי טעמא, ואייתר ליה "כי יסיר" לרבות שאר אומות. אלא לרבנן, איצטריך קרא לפרושי טעמא בז' אומות גופייהו, ולמעוטי שאר אומות, שאינן אדוקין בעבודת כוכבים כמותן, כדקי"ל (חולין דף יג:): אומות שבחוצה לארץ לאו עובדי עבודת כוכבים הן, אלא מנהג אבותיהם בידיהם; ולא אייתר ליה ריבויא, ושאר אומות מנלן? ודכוותיה אמר בסנהדרין (דף כא.) גבי "לא ירבה לו נשים ולא יסור לבבו", דלר"ש הוי האי "לא יסור" יתורא, דבלאו פירושא דקרא הוי דרשי' ביה טעמא; ולרבנן, דלא דרשינן טעמא דקרא בעלמא, הכא פריש קרא טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:7:1.english: Who expounds the reason of the verse - In Bava Metzia (115a), regarding a widow, where [Rabbi Shimon] says: [From] a wealthy [widow] one may take a pledge, [but from] a poor [widow] one may not take a pledge. For what is the reason the Merciful One stated, "You shall not take a widow’s garment in pledge" (Deuteronomy 24:17)? Because you must return her pledge to her in the evening, and as a result of your constantly entering and leaving her [home] — in the morning to take a pledge and in the evening to return [it] — you bring a bad name upon her among her neighbors. And so too [here, Rabbi Shimon] expounds the reason for [the prohibition against] intermarriage as being because "he will turn away [your son]" (Deuteronomy 7:4), and it was not necessary for the verse to explain the reason; thus, [the phrase] "for he will turn away" became superfluous for him, to include the other nations. But according to the Rabbis, the verse was necessary to explain the reason regarding the seven nations themselves, and to exclude the other nations, who are not as devoted to idol worship as they are — as we hold (Chullin 13b): The gentiles outside the Land [of Israel] are not idolaters, but rather [merely observe] the custom of their ancestors in their hands — and [thus] no inclusion was left superfluous for them; and regarding the other nations, from where do we [derive the prohibition]? And similarly, [the Gemara] says in Sanhedrin (21a) regarding "He shall not multiply wives for himself, that his heart not turn away" (Deuteronomy 17:17): that according to Rabbi Shimon, this [clause] "that [his heart] not turn away" is superfluous, because even without the verse’s explanation, we would have expounded a reason for it; whereas according to the Rabbis, who do not expound the reason of the verse generally, here the verse [specifically] explained the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:8:1.hebrew: ואחר כן - לאחר שתשהא כפי גזירת הכתוב שהתיר לך יפת תואר, "והיתה לך" כתיב — דריש בה הויה; אבל מעיקרא, קודם היתר, לא קרינן בה "והיתה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:8:1.english: And after that - After she waits in accordance with the decree of the verse that permitted a beautiful captive woman to you, it is written: “And she shall be to you” [Deuteronomy 21:13], [from which] it expounds *havayah* [betrothal] regarding her; but at the outset, prior to [this] permission, we do not read concerning her “and she shall be.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:9:1.english: And they have borne him - That [the child] traces his lineage after his father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 68b:9:2.english: We do not read concerning him, “And they have borne him” - Rather, [the child] traces his lineage after her.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:1:1.hebrew: ולדה כמוה מנלן - לפום ריהטא משמע דה"פ: נימא דישראל הבא על השפחה הולד כשר? והיכי נוכל להכשיר באין קידושין ויש עבירה יותר מיש קידושין ויש עבירה, ואמר דהולד הולך אחר הפגום?! וכי תימא דאתא לאשמועינן דאפי' בא עליה ממזר הולד כמוה, ויש לו תקנה בשחרור — הא ליתא אלא לרבי טרפון (לקמן קידושין דף סט.), אבל לרבנן לא. ונראה דה"פ: "ולדה כמוה מנא לן" — שלא יהא קרוי בנו לשום דבר, ואפילו כבנו ממזר לא הוי: לא ליורשו, ולא לטמא לו, ולא לייבם אשת אחיו, ולא לפטור אשת אביו מיבום:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:1:1.english: “Her offspring is like her, from where do we [derive this]?” - At first glance, it implies that this is its explanation: Would we say that [if] an Israelite has relations with a [Canaanite] maidservant, the offspring is fit? But how could we declare [the offspring] fit in [a case where] there is no betrothal and there is a transgression, more than [in a case where] there is betrothal and there is a transgression, regarding which [the Mishnah] states that the offspring follows the flawed [party]?! And if you should say that it comes to teach us that even if a mamzer had relations with her, the offspring is like her [in status as a slave] and has a remedy through emancipation — that is only according to Rabbi Tarfon (below, Kiddushin 69a), but according to the Rabbis, [that is] not [so]. And it appears that this is its explanation: “From where do we derive that her offspring is like her?” — [meaning,] that he should not be called his son for any matter, and he is not even like his son who is a mamzer: neither to inherit from him, nor [for a priest] to defile himself for him, nor to perform levirate marriage with his brother’s wife, nor to exempt his father’s wife from levirate marriage.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:2:1.hebrew: אמר קרא לא תתחתן בם - פירש בקונטרס: "לא יהא לך בהם תורת חתנות". מיהו קשה, שהרי האי קרא לא מיירי בעובדי כוכבים, דהא גבי ז' עממים הוא דכתיב, כדאמר בפרק הערל (יבמות דף עו.): אמר רבא, בגרותן אית להו חתנות — פירוש: איסור "לא תתחתן" יש בהם; ובגיותן לית להן חתנות — לא שייך בהו חתנות לעבור עליו משום "לא תתחתן". לכך פר"ת, דגמרא דמייתי קרא "לא תתחתן" הוי כמו וגומר, ומסיפא דקרא דריש, דכתיב: "בתך לא תתן לבנו ובתו לא תקח לבנך", משמע שאין בה קיחה. והקשה ה"ר יעקב מאורלינ"ש: ואימא ה"מ לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד תפסי בה קידושין, דכה"ג אמר לעיל (קידושין דף סז.) גבי "לא יקח איש את אשת אביו"? ותירץ מהר"ר יצחק שי"ש: דאין ה"נ, אלא סמך א"לא תתחתן" וא"לא תקח", דהוי כמו תרי קראי — חד לכתחילה וחד לדיעבד. ואע"ג דאמר "לא תתחתן" איירי בגירות, ה"מ בתר דידענא מסקנא דילפינן דלא תפסי בה קדושין מקרא אחרינא לקמן בסמוך; אבל אי לאו הכי, טוב היה לאוקמא קרא ד"לא תתחתן" לומר דלא תפסי בה קידושין, מלאוקמא בגירות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:2:1.english: The verse states: "Neither shall you make marriages with them" - Rashi explained: You shall have no validity of marriage with them. However, this is difficult, for this verse is not dealing with idol worshippers [in general], as it is written regarding the seven nations, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] He'arel (Yevamot 76a): Rava said: In their state of conversion, marriage applies to them — the explanation being: the prohibition of "neither shall you make marriages" applies to them; and in their state of gentiles, marriage does not apply to them — the concept of marriage is not applicable to them to transgress on account of "neither shall you make marriages." Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that when the Gemara cites the verse "neither shall you make marriages," it is like [saying] "and so forth"; and from the end of the verse it derives [this], as it is written: "Your daughter you shall not give to his son, nor his daughter shall you take to your son" [Deuteronomy 7:3], which implies that there is no taking [effective betrothal] with her. And Rabbi Yaakov of Orléans questioned: But [why not] say that this applies ab initio, but after the fact betrothal takes effect with her, as [the Gemara] said similarly above (Kiddushin 67a) regarding "A man shall not take his father's wife" [Deuteronomy 23:1]? And our teacher, Rabbi Yitzchak, may he live, answered: That indeed, it is so, but rather [the Gemara] relied upon "neither shall you make marriages" and "nor... shall you take," so that they are like two verses — one ab initio and one after the fact. And even though [Rava] said that "neither shall you make marriages" deals with [their state of] conversion, this applies only after we know the conclusion [of the Gemara] where we derive that betrothal is ineffective with her from another verse shortly below; but were it not so, it would have been better to establish the verse "neither shall you make marriages" to mean that betrothal is ineffective with her, rather than establishing it [as referring] to [their state of] conversion.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:3:1.hebrew: בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך - פי' בקונטרס: דכתיב: "כי יסיר את בנך מאחרי", דקאי א"בתך לא תתן לבנו"; וה"ק: בתך לא תתן לבנו, משום דכי יסיר בנו בן בתך מאחרי, והוא קרוי בנך. אבל בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים ומבנך אינו קרוי בנך אלא בנה, מדלא קאמר על "בתו לא תקח לבנך": כי תסיר בנך מאחרי. "אמר רבינא שמע מינה (בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים) כו'" — [וא"ת]: רבינא היינו דברי רבי יוחנן! ומה בא לחדש רבינא מה שלא פירש רבי יוחנן, דקאמר רבינא "שמע מינה"? לכך פירש רבינו תם: ד"כי יסיר את בנך" קאי א"בתו לא תקח לבנך", וה"ק: כי יסיר החותן את בנך, שהוא חתנו, מאחרי. ומדלא חש הכתוב על בן הבן, שמע מינה: בנך הנולד לך מאשתך קרוי בנך, לפי שהוא מישראל ומישראלית, ואין אותו הבא מבנך ומן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה. ודייק מלישנא ד"כי יסיר את בנך", דמשמע מיעוט, וממעט בן בנך, מדלא כתיב "כי יסירם" או "כי יסיר את זרעך". אבל אכתי לא ידענא מעובד כוכבים הבא על ישראלית מה דינו. ואתא רבינא וקאמר: שמע מינה בן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך, מדלא כתיב גבי "בתך לא תתן לבנו": "כי יסיר את בתך מאחרי", ונידוק מינה דעליה הקפיד רחמנא, כדדייקינן גבי "בתו לא תקח לבנך". ומדלא קאמר הכי, שמע מינה דבן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך, והקפיד קרא אתרוייהו; ולכך לא כתב "כי יסיר את בתך מאחרי", דמשמע מיעוט מבן בתו. עוד פר"ת: ד"כי יסיר" קאי א"בתו לא תקח לבנך", כדמפרש אחותן קאי, וה"ק: כי יסיר החותן את בנך מאחרי — שאין הזרע הבא מהן מתייחס אחר בנך, אלא אחר העובדת כוכבים; והיינו דאמר: "ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך", והיא הסרה דקאמר קרא. ובנך הבא מן הישראלית קרוי בנך דקאמר שמואל ורבי יוחנן (ביבמות דף יז.), לא פירשו כלום בעובד כוכבים הבא על בת ישראל, דמילתייהו בישראל הבא מן הישראלית שבעלה ישראל קאמר דהוי בנך. ורבינא בא לדקדק: שמע מינה בן בתך הבא מן העובד כוכבים קרוי בנך, מדלא כתיב "כי יסיר את בתך", שמע מינה דבתך הנשואה לעובד כוכבים ליכא הסרה, שהזרע מתייחס אחריה. ופי' זה קשה לר"י, ד"כי יסיר" משמע דמיירי בהסרת יראת שמים, כדדרשינן: "כי יסיר" לרבות כל המסירים, ומתרגמינן: "ארי יטעון ית בנך מבתר דחלתי". לכך נראה כפר"ת ראשון שפיר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:3:1.english:
Your son who comes from a Jewish woman is called your son - Rashi explained that it is written: "For he will turn away your son from following Me" (Deuteronomy 7:4), which refers to [the preceding clause]: "Your daughter you shall not give to his son" (Deuteronomy 7:3); and this is what it means: "Your daughter you shall not give to his son" because his son [the gentile son-in-law] will turn away your daughter's son from following Me, and he [your daughter's son] is called "your son." However, your son [i.e., your grandson] who comes from the gentile woman and from your son is not called your son, but her son, since [the Torah] did not state regarding "Nor his daughter shall you take for your son": "for she will turn away your son from following Me."
[As for that which] Ravina said: "Learn from this: [the son of your daughter born to a gentile is called your son] etc." — [if you will say]: Ravina's statement is the same as Rabbi Yoḥanan's words! What did Ravina come to innovate that Rabbi Yoḥanan did not [already] explain, that Ravina says "Learn from this"?
Therefore Rabbeinu Tam explained that "For he will turn away your son" refers to "Nor his daughter shall you take for your son"; and this is what it means: for the father-in-law [the gentile father of the bride] will turn away your son, who is his son-in-law, from following Me. And from [the fact] that Scripture was not concerned about the son's son [the grandchild born from the gentile daughter-in-law], learn from this: your son born to you from your wife is called "your son" because he is from a Jewish man and a Jewish woman, but that [grandchild] who comes from your son and from the gentile woman is not called your son, but her son. And [Rabbi Yoḥanan] deduces [this] from the wording "for he will turn away your son," which implies a limitation and excludes your son's son, since it is not written: "for he will turn them away" or "for he will turn away your offspring."
However, we would still not know what the status is regarding a gentile who has relations with a Jewish woman. And Ravina came and said: Learn from this that your daughter's son who comes from the gentile is called "your son," since it is not written regarding "Your daughter you shall not give to his son": "for he will turn away your daughter from following Me," from which we would have inferred that the Merciful One was concerned only about her, as we inferred regarding "Nor his daughter shall you take for your son." And since it did not say this, learn from this that your daughter's son who comes from the gentile is called "your son," and Scripture was concerned about both of them [the daughter and her child]; and therefore it did not write "for he will turn away your daughter from following Me," which would have implied the exclusion of the daughter's son.
Rabbeinu Tam furthermore explained that "for he will turn away" refers to "Nor his daughter shall you take for your son," as explained [above that] it refers to the father-in-law; and this is what it means: "for the father-in-law will turn away your son from following Me" — that the offspring who comes from them is not genealogically linked to your son, but rather to the gentile woman; and that is what [Rabbi Yoḥanan] said: "and your son who comes from the gentile woman is not called your son," and this [severing of lineage] is the "turning away" of which Scripture speaks. And [as for the principle]: "your son who comes from a Jewish woman is called your son," where Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan stated [in Yevamot 17a], they did not explain anything about a gentile who has relations with a daughter of Israel, for their statement was [only] regarding a Jew born of a Jewish woman whose husband is a Jew, stating that he is your son. And Ravina came to deduce: Learn from this that your daughter's son who comes from the gentile is called your son, since it is not written "for he will turn away your daughter" — learn from this that regarding your daughter who is married to a gentile, there is no "turning away," for the offspring is genealogically linked to her.
And this explanation is difficult to the Ri, for "for he will turn away" implies that it deals with turning away from the fear of Heaven, as we expound: "'for he will turn away' — to include all who turn [someone] away," and we translate [in the Targum]: "For he will lead your son astray from following My fear [worship]." Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam's first explanation appears sound.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:7:1.hebrew: הניחא לר"ש - פי': דדריש טעמא דקראי, ה"נ אמר טעמא דחיתון — דאי לא כתיב "כי יסיר", ה"א מסברא דמיירי משבעה עממים, לפי שהם אדוקין בעבודת כוכבים יותר משאר אומות, ולפיכך "לא תתחתן", וכתב רחמנא "כי יסיר" לרבות כל המסירין. אלא לרבנן דלא דרשי טעמא דקרא, א"כ אי לאו קרא יתירא, ה"א "לא תתחתן" מיירי בכל האומות, ואיצטריך "כי יסיר" לומר דוקא בשבעה עממים; א"כ, בשאר אומות מנליה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 68b:7:1.english: "This works out well according to Rabbi Shimon" - Explanation: Because he expounds the reason of the verses, here too he stated the reason for intermarriage: For had it not been written, "For he will turn away", I would have said through logic that it is dealing with the seven nations, because they are more devoted to idolatry than other nations, and therefore "You shall not intermarry"; and the Merciful One wrote "For he will turn away" to include all who turn one away. But according to the Rabbis, who do not expound the reason of the verse, if so, were it not for an extra verse, I would have said "You shall not intermarry" is dealing with all the nations, and "For he will turn away" was necessary to say specifically regarding the seven nations; if so, in regard to the other nations, from where do they derive the prohibition?
